mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in demand and construction, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers long-term interest rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 persons per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market absorption and economic expansion, which supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 persons per month for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer purchasing power and deflationary pressure, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and CPIAUCSL both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and CPIAUCSL decline for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
